newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish PAP agency sees profits after 2-year reform.
newsitem.headline: Polish PAP agency sees profits after 2-year reform.

text.p: Poland's state-owned news agency, Polska Agencja Prasowa (PAP), plans to start generating profits after a two-year transformation period leading to its partial privatisation, the agency's president said on Monday.

Krzysztof Komornicki told a news conference that PAP, now subsidised by the central budget, would aim to become financially independent thanks to cost-cutting and higher revenues from sales of new services.
"PAP's financial reform and gaining independence...will mean first of all efforts to increase revenues, through providing better service and its diversification," Krzysztof Komornicki said on Monday.

Komornicki told reporters that the national agency wanted to phase out state subsidies and break even in two years after it is transformed into a treasury joint-stock company, a move planned at the start of 1998.
Komornicki said the agency planned a growth of revenues offering new products such as a specialised financial service, graphics service and advertising section via internet.
Poland's parliament has already passed a bill authorising the government to sell up to 49 percent of the news agency.
PAP will be managed in line with Poland's commercial code, except that its first president and board will be chosen by the Treasury minister and approved by the prime minister.
